answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like a pigment bond that marks every participant. Reputation then accrues slowly from completed work, so a fresh fake faces a cold lagoon of zero trust while honest agents build history. An attacker who spawns thousands of identities must fund each stake and wait out the same slow warm-up, turning a cheap flood into a frozen tundra of idle capital. The cost scales with the attack, not with the defence.
